info.name: OBP B2C - Auth0 End-to-End (UC-01..UC-15)
info.description:
Drives every B2C use case against Auth0 with no front end and no real core.

**Before you run it**
1. `cd mocks/dna-mock && npm install && npm start`, then tunnel it so Auth0 can reach it.
2. `make apply ENV=dev STACK=b2c && make apply ENV=dev STACK=tenant`.
3. `make output ENV=dev STACK=b2c` and copy the ids into the environment file.

**How it works**
The `test_harness` client enables the resource-owner password-realm grant, which is what makes headless testing possible. That client exists only in dev and qa, and stacks/b2c refuses to create it in prod.

Three requests are marked BROWSER STEP. They exercise `api.redirect` and interactive step-up, which have no headless equivalent - open them in a browser rather than pressing Send.

item.name: 00 - Setup
item.description: Run this folder first. It resets the mock to seed state and mints a Management API token used by the support use cases.

request.description: Uses the support_m2m client created by stacks/b2c. Its grants are declared in Terraform, so a missing scope here means the tfvars need updating, not the Dashboard.

item.name: UC-01 - User Registration
item.description: CIF is validated against the core by the pre-user-registration Action before any Auth0 user exists. A 5-digit CIF is a bank customer, 6-digit is trust.

exec: pm.test('auth0 user id returned', () => pm.expect(b._id || b.email).to.exist);

request.description: The signup payload carries the CIF in user_metadata. The pre-user-registration Action reads it, calls POST /members/verify-cif, and promotes it to app_metadata so the customer can never edit it.
In a real run the customer clicks the link in the verify_email template. Here we set the flag directly so the rest of the suite can proceed unattended.

item.name: UC-02 - New User Login
item.description: Headless login via the resource-owner password-realm grant. This grant exists only on the non-production test harness client - it is not how VeriChannel authenticates.

item.name: Login succeeds and carries custom claims
Login with the wrong password fails

exec: pm.test('no account state disclosed', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.match(/locked|does not exist/i));

request.description: The trust user from UC-01 was never verified, so the access-control Action denies at post-login. This is UC-02 Req-5.

exec: // Requires 'Trust Token Endpoint IP Header' on the harness client.

request.description: auth0-forwarded-for is only honoured when the client has is_token_endpoint_ip_header_trusted set. If this test is inconclusive, verify the rule in the browser through a VPN instead - the Action logic is identical.

item.name: UC-03 - Legacy User Login
item.description: The legacy population lives in Fiserv DNA and is identified by username. Auth0 imports each user on first successful login (import_mode = true).

item.name: Legacy user with a verified email migrates silently
Core saw exactly one authenticate call
Second login does not touch the core

request.description: Proves the import worked: the user now authenticates against Auth0's own store, and the identifier is the email rather than the username.

item.name: Legacy user without an email is flagged for collection

request.description: A redirect Action cannot run under the password grant, so the Action stamps app_metadata.email_collection_required instead. The full redirect + OTP flow must be exercised in a browser - see the note below.

item.name: Confirm the collection flag was set

exec: pm.test('reference only - open this URL in a browser', () => true);

request.description:
Do not run this with Send. Copy the URL into a browser and sign in as jdoe1978 / Legacy#Pass2019.

Expected: Universal Login -> redirect to the mock form -> enter an address -> OTP (printed in the mock console and served at GET {{mock_base_url}}/_admin/otp/<auth0-user-id>) -> back to /continue -> authorization code.

This is the only UC-03 path that exercises api.redirect, so it stays a manual gate until VeriChannel ships the real screen.

item.name: UC-04 & UC-05 - Step-Up and MFA Factors
item.description: MFA is driven from the post-login Action, not from a tenant-wide policy, so step-up and risk-based challenges share one code path. Email OTP and TOTP are the Phase-1 factors; SMS is deliberately absent.

request.description: Set always_on_mfa = true in the dev tfvars before running this folder, otherwise a low-risk login is not challenged and there is no mfa_token to work with.

exec: pm.test('barcode returned for the enrolment screen', () => pm.expect(b.barcode_uri || b.secret).to.exist);
pm.test('amr includes an mfa method', () => pm.expect(claims[ns + '/amr'].join(',')).to.match(/mfa|otp|email/));

request.description: Set email_otp_code from the inbox (or from the Auth0 log stream in dev). This is the assertion that proves UC-04 acceptance: the token's acr changes only after a real second factor.

item.name: BROWSER STEP - step-up for a high-risk action

request.description:
How VeriChannel asks for step-up on each of the six Fraud Team actions: a fresh /authorize with acr_values + prompt=login + obp_action=<name>.

Valid obp_action values: update_profile, manage_etransfer_recipients, manage_interac_profile, manage_bill_payees, cra_direct_deposit, manage_delegates.

The Action disables browser remembering for step-up, so the challenge always appears, and posts a STEP_UP_REQUESTED security event - assert on it in the next request.

item.name: Step-up was notified to the core
UC-06 - Account Lockout
item.description: Three consecutive failures lock the account. Auth0 brute-force protection does the locking; the notification email is the blocked_account template.

item.name: Fourth attempt is throttled even with the right password

request.description: Correct credentials must still fail. If this passes with a 200, brute_force_max_attempts in environments/<env>/tenant.tfvars did not apply, or the runner IP is on the allowlist.

exec: pm.test('no account state leaked to the caller', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include('ACCOUNT_LOCKED'));

request.description: The mock returns 423 and the login script maps it to a generic UnauthorizedError. The customer learns nothing about the account from an unauthenticated call.

item.name: UC-07 - Self-Service Password Reset
item.description: The reset link lives 15 minutes, enforces 12+ characters with four character classes, blocks reuse of the last 24 passwords, and lifts the lockout from UC-06.

item.name: Unknown address gets the same answer

exec: pm.test('same status as a known address', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('no enumeration signal', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.match(/not found|does not exist/i));

request.description: UC-07 acceptance: no PII revealed to an unauthorised user. The two responses above must be indistinguishable.
ttl_sec 900 is the 15-minute acceptance criterion expressed at the API. Agents never see or set a password.

item.name: Reset lifted the lock and told the core
UC-08 & UC-09 - Profile, Sessions and Device Activity
item.description: Profile writes that matter to fraud require a fresh step-up first. Session and login history come from the Management API and are surfaced by the portal.

exec: pm.test('CIF is in app_metadata, not user_metadata', () => {

request.description: app_metadata is not writable by the customer. If the CIF ever appears in user_metadata after registration, the pre-user-registration Action has regressed.
This is the feed the portal renders as 'recent activity'. Filter to the success/failure login codes (s, f, ssa, fp) before showing it to a customer.

item.name: UC-10 & UC-11 - Delegated Admin and Notifications
item.description: Delegation is role-scoped and time-bound. Every notification the customer receives has a matching security event at the core.

request.description: role_delegated_admin_id comes from `make output ENV=dev STACK=b2c` -> role_ids.olb_delegated_admin.

item.name: Delegation window is recorded on the delegate

request.description: Auth0 roles have no expiry, so the window lives in app_metadata and the post-login Action drops the delegate role once expiresAt has passed. Keep that logic in one place.

exec: pm.test('each event names a customer', () => pm.expect(e.every(x => x.cif || x.auth0UserId)).to.be.true);

item.name: UC-12, UC-14, UC-15 - Support-Initiated Flows
item.description: Agents act through the Management API with a narrow scope set. No agent ever sees or sets a password, and every action is attributable.

item.name: UC-12 - trigger a password reset for the customer

request.description: Both the Auth0 `blocked` flag and the app_metadata reason are set: the flag stops the login, the metadata explains it to the next agent and to the auditor.

item.name: UC-14 - locked customer cannot sign in

request.description: Distinct from the `blocked` flag. UC-06 lockouts are IP/identifier blocks and are cleared here or by a successful SSPR.

item.name: UC-15 - customer can sign in again

request.description: A 403 with error=mfa_required is also a pass: it means access was restored and MFA is doing its job.

item.name: Support actions are in the audit trail
